Sibuna 1.0.0-rc.3 fixes how reputation reaches the nodes of the firewall daemon, with PostgreSQL in a cluster and with SQLite on one node (issue #2).

Until now every ban, lift or operator's reputation row rebuilt the whole policy engine on every node. The engine kept reputation in a trie of 8,192 nodes, so once a few hundred to a few thousand addresses were banned every rebuild failed, and a node stopped applying the operator's policy changes. Reputation is now published beside the engine. Each write of ip_reputation is stamped by a counter that writers take in commit order, and each node applies only the changes after the last one it applied. One change to a set of a million addresses costs about 2 microseconds; a million IPv4 addresses take about 50 MiB. Bans end on time without a database read, and a policy change no longer reads reputation. No request waits for any of this. SID 0033 specifies the design, and a Lean model proves that the node's set equals the table.

Core migration 3 adds the change log. In a cluster we upgrade all nodes together: a node of an older version does not see new bans after the migration.

The book's figures are redrawn, and the operations chapter describes how a policy or reputation change reaches the nodes, in all eight languages.

The release uses Rust 1.100.0. The optional OpenBSD 7.9 amd64 package uses the system Rust 1.94.1 and is attached after native package checks pass. SHA256SUMS lists the published assets.
